STAGE 1 - design-space selection
GOAL: pick a coupling position for training-only behaviour x hyperbolic geometry that no earlier round used and that is not a copy of an existing repo mechanism.
READ: the task brief, the three earlier rounds (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID/prefix-transition curvature, BRad-RQ radial behaviour-ranked assignment, plus Lorentz successor smoothing, behaviour-cone prefix RQ, succboost geoshift, branchcurv-MoE) and the workspace listing (only session/progress files, no repository code present here, so no local mechanism can be copied).
OBSERVED: all earlier rounds couple behaviour to (a) codebook centroid updates (Frechet), (b) per-level curvature scalars, (c) radial/ranking of assignment, (d) first-order embedding shifts/cones. None uses a pure curvature invariant - the holonomy (angle defect) of a geodesic triangle - as the operator, and none acts on the tangent frame of the residual.
EVIDENCE: round summaries quoted in the prompt; workspace glob returned only session.jsonl, progress.jsonl, running.json, opencode.json, stderr.log.
REASONING: a Gauss-Bonnet angle defect is exactly zero in flat space AND exactly zero when the behaviour point collapses onto the prefix, so behaviour and curvature are not additive contributions but a single interaction term. That is the strongest possible form of the required coupling, and it sits in the quantizer (assignment) rather than in the codebook update, which is an unoccupied position for this round.
OPEN: verify the hyperbolic law-of-cosines angle formulas, the principal-angle safeguard, and the per-step cost at 24556 items / 24 steps / 3000 epochs.

STAGE 2 - mathematical and cost verification of HOLO-DETOUR-RQ
GOAL: check that the proposed operator is well defined, numerically safe, has no tunable constant, and is cheap enough for the frozen budget.
READ: standard Poincare-ball identities (Mobius addition, exp/log maps, d_c = 2/sqrt(c) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)+y||)), the hyperbolic law of cosines for curvature -c, Gauss-Bonnet (angle defect = c * area), and the SO(2) rotation formula in a 2-plane.
OBSERVED: (i) the triangle angles are computable from the three side lengths alone, so only three distances are needed; (ii) delta = pi - (alpha_O+alpha_P+alpha_M) is in (0,pi) and its principal value in [0,pi/2] is a valid quarter-turn bound derived from geometry, not tuned; (iii) because the Poincare metric is conformal with isotropic factor lambda_p, a Euclidean-orthogonal 2-plane rotation in coordinate tangent space is also hyperbolic-orthogonal, so the rotation preserves the tangent norm and exp_p(r') stays on the same geodesic sphere as z; (iv) with m(p)=p the triangle is degenerate, delta=0; with c->0 the defect is c*area ->0, so both switches correctly collapse to the plain hyperbolic RQ.
EVIDENCE: derivations above, done analytically in this session; no external file needed.
REASONING: cost per (item, level) is ~3 distances + 3 angle evaluations (~O(100) flops) + one O(d) 2-plane rotation, with d~64. Batch ~1023, L=4 -> ~8e6 flops/step of extra forward work plus small autograd overhead, i.e. a low-single-digit percentage of a transformer step. Per-epoch cluster-mean refresh is 24556 log/exp, sub-second. No coupling weight exists to sweep; the only constants are c=1 (unit-ball normalisation), epsilon guards, the principal-angle bound pi/2, and K=3 Karcher iterations (documented deterministic defaults).
OPEN: none blocking; the proposal is fully specified and in scope.

STAGE 3a - final answer part 1/3 (HOLO-DETOUR-RQ)
GOAL: deliver the single in-scope idea, one block, required field format; split across records because of the 4000-character record limit.
READ: nothing new; assembles stages 1-2.
OBSERVED: answer text part 1 follows.
EVIDENCE: verbatim answer below; stages 1-2 hold the justification and verification.
OPEN: parts 2/3 and 3/3 carry the rest.

IDEA: HOLO-DETOUR-RQ
TITLE: Geodesic-holonomy residual rotation: the behaviour successor mean bends the RQ tangent frame by the curvature angle defect
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE prefixes are learned purely from reconstruction, so two items with the same prefix can have completely different training-time next items. A generative recommender then emits a prefix whose continuation distribution is behaviourally incoherent. The problem is that nothing in the quantizer knows where the prefix actually leads. This idea makes the prefix's own training-transition successors define a second, curved path from the origin to the prefix, and lets the curvature-induced mismatch between the direct path and the behaviour-detour path rotate the residual that selects the next code. Prefixes therefore become frames aligned with their behavioural future rather than only with reconstruction.
NOVELTY: The operator is a pure curvature invariant, the Gauss-Bonnet angle defect (holonomy) of the geodesic triangle (origin, prefix point, behaviour successor mean), applied as an SO(2) rotation of the residual tangent vector before the nearest-code search. Earlier work here coupled behaviour through codebook centroids (Frechet), per-level curvature scalars, radial/rank assignment, cones, and first-order embedding shifts; none used a frame/holonomy term, and none sits at the level of the residual's tangent frame. The rotation is exactly zero both in flat space and when the behaviour point collapses onto the prefix, so the behaviour term and the curvature term are not two additive losses but a single multiplicative interaction that exists only when both are on.
CHANGE: At every RQ level the residual r_l = log_{p_l}(z) is rotated by R(delta_l), where delta_l is the angle defect of the geodesic triangle O-p_l-m(p_l) under curvature -c and m(p_l) is the training-transition successor mean of the items currently sharing prefix p_l. The rotated residual, not the raw one, is compared with the level codebook, so the chosen code (and therefore the whole downstream prefix) depends jointly on behaviour and curvature.
SPECIFICATION: Poincare ball B^d_c with fixed c=1 (embeddings projected to ||x|| <= (1-eps)/sqrt(c)); exp/log/Mobius-add as usual. For each level l: p_0 = g = Frechet mean of training item embeddings; r_l = log_{p_l}(z); m(p_l) = exp_0( sum_{i in C(p_l)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ); compute a=d_c(p_l,m), b=d_c(O,m), d=d_c(O,p_l); angles by the curvature -c law of cosines; delta_l = pi - (alpha_O + alpha_P + alpha_M), principal value clamped to [0, pi/2]; build the orthonormal 2-frame u = log_0(p_l)/||log_0(p_l)||, w = orthonormalised part of log_0(m) orthogonal to u; r'_l = R(delta_l) r_l with R = I + sin(delta)(w u^T - u w^T) + (cos(delta)-1)(u u^T + w w^T); code k_l = argmin_k d_c(exp_{p_l}(r'_l), e_{l,k}); p_{l+1} = p_l (+) e_{l,k_l}. All delta and m values are stop-gradient; gradients flow through r_l in z and p_l.

STAGE 3b - final answer part 2/4 (HOLO-DETOUR-RQ)
Continuation of the single answer block; cost through risks.

COST: Frozen scale is 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch (about 1023 items/step), 3000 epochs, four cards, one run. Per step the extra work is about 1023 x 4 levels x (3 distances + 3 angle evaluations + one 64-dim 2-plane rotation) ~ 8e6 flops, roughly 1-3 percent of a transformer step, plus a small autograd node count for the exp/log maps. The per-epoch prefix-cluster successor refresh is 24556 log/exp plus 4 aggregations, under a second. Per-item successor means are precomputed once at epoch 0 and refreshed every 100 Stage-2 epochs from detached embeddings (about 7e5 exp/log per refresh, tens of seconds total). Expected wall-clock overhead 2-5 percent; the 3000-epoch budget, the frozen Stage-3 protocol and the single run are unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: If the RQ tangent frame at a prefix is rotated toward the direction of that prefix's training-transition successors, deeper codes become more behaviour-predictable and the generative recommender should place the true next item inside its top-10 beam more often. Keep condition: on the single run Stage-3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065, with recorded diagnostics showing (i) measurable churn in level>=1 code assignments, (ii) higher prefix-to-successor top-1 predictability on training prefixes, (iii) no collapse of codebook usage. If recall is flat while delta_l is empirically near zero for most prefixes, the behaviour means are too close to the prefix and the idea is doing nothing.
RISKS: (a) delta_l near zero for most prefixes, making the rotation a no-op; (b) delta_l near pi/2 for a minority could over-rotate and scramble good codes; (c) the successor mean is dominated by globally popular continuations unless the count normalisation suppresses them; (d) rotating the target on its geodesic sphere changes only assignment, not the reconstruction target, so the codebook may keep its old geometry and the gain may be limited; (e) a per-epoch behaviour statistic is a moving target that can slow convergence inside the fixed 3000 epochs.

STAGE 3c - final answer part 3/4 (HOLO-DETOUR-RQ)
Continuation of the single answer block; behaviour signal through hyperbolic location.

BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transitions inside training sequences (the immediate next items within a forward window of 5 positions), turned into a normalised transition weight and then into a per-prefix successor mean point in the Poincare ball.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, build a sparse table count(i -> y) over next-item pairs inside a window of 5 in each training sequence. Set w(i,y) = count(i,y) / sqrt(pop(i) * pop(y)) with pop(x) the total training occurrence count (a cosine/popularity normalisation with no free parameter). The per-item successor point is m_i = argmin_{m in B} sum_y w(i,y) d_c(m, e_y)^2, solved by K=3 Karcher fixed-point iterations m <- exp_m( sum_y w(i,y) log_m(e_y) / sum_y w(i,y) ) from m = e_i, using current detached item embeddings. The prefix successor point is m(p) = exp_0( sum_{i in C(p)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ) with w_i = out-degree of i in the training transition graph and C(p) the items assigned prefix p at the previous epoch's snapshot. Items with no training successors take m_i = e_i; prefixes with fewer than two members or with m(p) within 1e-3 of p take delta = 0.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition table, popularity counts, per-item successor means and per-prefix means are built exclusively from the training split's user sequences; validation and test interactions are never read, and the Stage-3 protocol only consumes the frozen SID table produced by Stage 2. No validation or test user, item or transition enters the curvature, the behaviour means, the frame construction or the code assignment. The per-epoch refresh uses current model parameters and the same frozen training transition weights, so it is a training-time statistic, not a data leak.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare-ball model of constant negative curvature -c with c = 1 fixed by the unit-ball normalisation (no curvature sweep). Curved operations used: Mobius addition, exp_p / log_p maps, geodesic distance d_c, the curvature -c hyperbolic law of cosines for triangle angles, the Gauss-Bonnet angle defect delta = pi - (alpha_O + alpha_P + alpha_M), and the resulting SO(2) holonomy rotation R(delta).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual quantizer, at every RQ level, after the residual r_l = log_{p_l}(z) is formed and before the nearest-code search; the rotation changes the code index and therefore the straight-through gradient and the SID prefix, and it runs in the forward pass of the reconstruction loss.

STAGE 3d - final answer part 4a (HOLO-DETOUR-RQ)
Continuation of the single answer block; coupling and switches.

COUPLING PATH: z -> p_l -> successor mean m(p_l) from the training transition table -> geodesic triangle (O, p_l, m(p_l)) -> angle defect delta_l under curvature c -> rotation R(delta_l) -> rotated residual r'_l -> nearest code k_l -> SID prefix p_{l+1} -> Stage-3 generation. Removing behaviour sets m(p_l) = p_l: the triangle degenerates and delta_l = 0, so R = I. Removing geometry sets c = 0: the defect is c * area = 0 and R = I as well, and exp/log/d_c become their Euclidean counterparts. The rotation therefore exists only when both factors are present, and one connected pathway carries both into the code index.
COUPLING EQUATION: r'_l = R( delta_c( O, p_l, m(p_l) ) ) * log_{p_l}(z), with delta_c = pi - ( alpha_O(c,a,b,d) + alpha_P(c,a,b,d) + alpha_M(c,a,b,d) ), a = d_c(p_l, m(p_l)), b = d_c(O, m(p_l)), d = d_c(O, p_l). Behaviour enters only through m(p_l) from the training transition table; curvature enters only through the sqrt(c)-scaled law of cosines and the metric d_c; the product R(delta) * log_{p_l}(z) is the single term where they meet.
OBSERVABLES: (i) per-level SID churn: fraction of items whose code at level l changes relative to the uncoupled quantizer, expected near zero at the root only if the root collapses and clearly nonzero at levels 1 and above; (ii) prefix-to-successor top-1 predictability of training prefixes under a held-out-transition probe, which should rise if the rotation aligns frames with behaviour; (iii) codebook usage entropy and collision rate as health checks; (iv) the primary judgement, Stage-3 test Recall@10 against 0.065 on the single frozen-protocol run.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: The same code with the transition table disabled: m(p_l) := p_l for every prefix, so every geodesic triangle is degenerate, delta_l = 0, R = I, and the quantizer reduces to the plain hyperbolic RQ. No other change.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: The same code with c = 0: exp/log become identity, d_c becomes Euclidean squared distance, the law of cosines is replaced by the flat one giving zero defect, and delta_l := 0 with R = I. Behaviour statistics are still computed and still attached, they simply cannot act.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run exactly as specified: training-only successor means build m(p_l), the curved triangle gives delta_l, and R(delta_l) rotates the residual at every RQ level. Nothing is ablated and nothing is tuned in this run; the switches exist in the code for later diagnosis but only this arm is trained.

STAGE 3e - final answer part 4b, closes the block (HOLO-DETOUR-RQ)
SPEC EQUATIONS: c=1. x (+) y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x + (1-c||x||^2)y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2). exp_0(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v/(sqrt(c)||v||); log_0(x)=artanh(sqrt(c)||x||) x/(sqrt(c)||x||). exp_p(v)=p (+)( tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_p ||v||/2) v/(sqrt(c)||v||) ), lambda_p=2/(1-c||p||^2). log_p(x)=(2/(sqrt(c) lambda_p)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-p)(+)x||) ((-p)(+)x)/||(-p)(+)x||. d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||). Law of cosines: cos alpha_O = (cosh(sqrt(c)b)cosh(sqrt(c)d) - cosh(sqrt(c)a)) / (sinh(sqrt(c)b)sinh(sqrt(c)d)), cyclically for alpha_P and alpha_M with the opposite side entering the first factor. delta = pi - (alpha_O+alpha_P+alpha_M); delta <- min(delta, pi-delta); delta <- clip(delta, 0, pi/2). u = log_0(p_l)/||log_0(p_l)||; wperp = log_0(m) - <log_0(m),u>u; w = wperp/||wperp||; R = I + sin(delta)(w u^T - u w^T) + (cos(delta)-1)(u u^T + w w^T). r_l = log_{p_l}(z); r'_l = R r_l; k_l = argmin_k d_c(exp_{p_l}(r'_l), e_{l,k}); p_{l+1} = p_l (+) e_{l,k_l}. Successor means: w(i,y)=count(i,y)/sqrt(pop(i)pop(y)); m_i from K=3 iterations m <- exp_m( sum_y w(i,y) log_m(e_y) / sum_y w(i,y) ); m(p)=exp_0( sum_{i in C(p)} w_i log_0(m_i) / sum_i w_i ), w_i = out-degree(i). Total loss is unchanged (RQ reconstruction + commitment + codebook) except that the codes and prefixes are the rotated ones.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs per item per level: item embedding z in B^d_c, current prefix point p_l in B^d_c, prefix successor mean m(p_l) in B^d_c (or p_l itself when behaviour is off), and level codebook {e_{l,k}} in B^d_c. Outputs: scalar holonomy angle delta_l, rotated tangent vector r'_l in R^d with the same hyperbolic norm as r_l, selected code index k_l, next prefix point p_{l+1}; and, with the switch off, delta_l = 0 and r'_l = r_l.
SAFEGUARDS: project every encoder output and codebook entry to ||x|| <= (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c) after each update; clamp artanh arguments to 1-1e-7 and cosh arguments to at most 20; set delta = 0 whenever any sinh(sqrt(c)a), sinh(sqrt(c)b), sinh(sqrt(c)d) is below 1e-6, whenever ||log_0(p_l)|| < 1e-3, whenever ||wperp|| < 1e-3, or whenever the prefix cluster has fewer than two members; take the principal defect min(delta, pi-delta) and clamp to [0, pi/2] so the rotation never exceeds a quarter turn; assert | ||r'_l|| - ||r_l|| | < 1e-6 because R is orthogonal in the conformal coordinate frame and the Poincare metric factor is isotropic; stop-gradient on delta_l and m(p_l) so no gradient is taken through acosh or through transition statistics; fall back to m_i = e_i for items with zero training successors; if a NaN appears in delta, reset it to 0 for that step and continue rather than aborting the run.
END IDEA

STAGE 3 COMPLETE. The four records 3a-3e concatenate, in order, to the full answer block: IDEA, TITLE, MOTIVATION, NOVELTY, CHANGE, SPECIFICATION, COST, HYPOTHESIS, RISKS, BEHAVIOR SIGNAL, BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION, LEAKAGE BOUNDARY, HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR, HYPERBOLIC LOCATION, COUPLING PATH, COUPLING EQUATION, OBSERVABLES, ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF, ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF, ABLATION BOTH ON, SPEC EQUATIONS, SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS, SAFEGUARDS, END IDEA.
Reasoning for the record: all five scope conditions are met; the defect is a pure interaction term so the coupling cannot be reduced to a behaviour suffix or a parallel loss; no coupling weight exists to sweep; only the both-on arm is trained; the budget and Stage-3 protocol are untouched; the cost at 24556 items / 24 steps / 24 epochs-per-1000 is a low-single-digit percentage overhead.
